concepts.def: Paley's watch analogy argues that order and purpose in nature, like the parts of a watch, point to an intelligent designer; an a posteriori argument.
Aquinas's first three Ways argue from motion, causation and contingency that the universe depends on an uncaused, necessary being - God.
Anselm defined God as 'that than which nothing greater can be conceived' and argued a priori that such a being must exist in reality.
Hume attacked the design analogy as weak, noted the universe is unique, and argued the evidence cannot establish one perfect, infinite designer.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Philosophy of Religion: Philosophical Issues & Questions — a core area of A-Level Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Philosophy of Religion: Philosophical Issues & Questions brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Philosophy of Religion: Philosophical Issues & Questions.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does Paley's watch analogy argue?
options: Complexity and purpose in nature imply a designer, just as a watch implies a watchmaker
Time proves the universe is eternal
Machines cannot ever be designed
Nature and watches are both undesigned

mcqs.q: Which argument for God's existence is a priori?
options: The ontological argument
The design argument
The cosmological argument
The argument from religious experience
That than which nothing greater can be conceived
The first cause of motion only
The soul of the universe
A being beyond all language

mcqs.q: Kant's claim that 'existence is not a predicate' is an objection to which argument?
options: The ontological argument
The design argument
The moral argument
The argument from miracles

mcqs.q: Did Hume claim to have proved that God does not exist?
options: Hume argued the design argument was completely irrefutable.
Hume's criticisms amount to a demonstration that there is no God.
No - Hume undermined the force of the design and causal arguments, but his Dialogues end ambiguously; weakening proofs is not the same as proving atheism.
The cosmological argument is based on the beauty of sunsets.

mcqs.q: Does the cosmological argument say 'everything has a cause, so God must have one too'?
options: Hume argued the design argument was completely irrefutable.
No - classical versions argue that things in motion or contingent things require explanation, concluding in a necessary, uncaused being; that being is not another contingent item needing a cause.
The cosmological argument is based on the beauty of sunsets.
The cosmological argument is refuted simply by asking 'then what caused God?'

mcqs.q: Does evolution automatically destroy every design argument?
options: It targets Paley-style biological design, but fine-tuning versions appeal to the constants of physics, so evaluation must match the criticism to the version of the argument.
Darwin ended all possible design reasoning about the universe.
Evolution disproved the cosmological argument about motion.
Hume argued the design argument was completely irrefutable.
